Step 3:
What to test next

Machine learning picks the experiments that would cut the model's uncertainty about Moon/Mars Exploration Atmosphere the most.

Material: Thin acrylic film (PMMA), air flowing against the flame. Change it in step 2.

Computational research candidates requiring qualified scientific review, established safety procedures and formal feasibility assessment.

Closest ISS test of this material: 22.2 % oxygen, 101.4 kPa (pressure assumed). That is 11.8 points of oxygen and 45 kPa from this cabin's air.

1
Test thin acrylic film (PMMA) at 34 % oxygen, 56.5 kPa (8.2 psia) and 1.7 cm/s airflow.

Would cut the model's uncertainty about this cabin by 19 %.

Why it matters: this is the air the crew would breathe. One test here would show directly whether the material keeps burning in it. Results like this inform what fire controls a cabin like this needs.

This is the cabin's own air. The most informative single test is at the cabin's own conditions. That follows from the model's assumption that conditions close together behave alike.

2
Test thin acrylic film (PMMA) at 34 % oxygen, 56.5 kPa (8.2 psia) and 13.2 cm/s airflow.

Would cut it by a further 14 % after test 1.

3
Test thin acrylic film (PMMA) at 34 % oxygen, 56.5 kPa (8.2 psia) and 45 cm/s airflow.

Would cut it by a further 10 % after tests 1 and 2.

These conditions are outside what ISS tests have demonstrated. Feasibility is not verified.
